builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Mechanistic Insights into LoRA: Layer Sparsity for Adaptive Fine-Tuning via Path Patching
summary: The method replaces standard all-layer LoRA, which fine-tunes every transformer layer, with LoRA applied only to task-relevant layers identified by a frozen-base zero-ablation calibration pass. It reduces adapter parameters roughly 3.5x while adding a per-task calibration step and per-task layer-selection bookkeeping; training compute per step is otherwise comparable to standard LoRA. Layer importance is reported as highly task-dependent with limited cross-task overlap, so a selection calibrated on one task or benchmark can underperform on another, and results are demonstrated on a single 1.5B model and may not transfer to other architectures, scales, or non-reasoning workloads.
rationale: The 3.5x adapter-parameter reduction is modest for inference-constrained deployments and rests on one small model and reasoning tasks, so the method warrants small-scale validation on the reader's own fine-tuning workload before adoption.

claims.statement: The method replaces standard all-layer LoRA, which fine-tunes every transformer layer, with LoRA applied only to task-relevant layers identified by a frozen-base zero-ablation calibration pass. It reduces adapter parameters roughly 3.5x while adding a per-task calibration step and per-task layer-selection bookkeeping; training compute per step is otherwise comparable to standard LoRA. Layer importance is reported as highly task-dependent with limited cross-task overlap, so a selection calibrated on one task or benchmark can underperform on another, and results are demonstrated on a single 1.5B model and may not transfer to other architectures, scales, or non-reasoning workloads.
Adaptive-LoRA outperforms full-layer LoRA while using only 30% of layers, achieving a 3.5x reduction in adapter parameters (Qwen2.5-1.5B, 11 reasoning tasks).
